Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

escape verb and noun

get away

also get away, break out, run away (from danger), flee, an escape, a way out, narrow escape, take to one’s heels, take to his heels, run for it, make a run for it

classical

Cic. Phil. 2, 29: ē proeliō (Lewis & Short)
Phaedr. 2.8.2
Traupman 56
Traupman 310

effugiō, effugere, effūgī

verb, third conjugation (-iō): with ex or ab + ablative, or with the accusative of the danger escaped

escape, get away

With the accusative of what one escapes (mortem effugere), or with ex of the place. Also simply to avoid or shun.

Other words

  • ēvādō, ēvādere, ēvāsī, ēvāsum — get out, get away safe

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Phaedr. 4.9.11: ēvāsit puteō

    Properly to come out (of the water, a building) or climb up; so, to get away safe (ē perīculō, Cic. Div. 2.13). It also means to turn out, end up.

  • aufugiō, aufugere, aufūgī — run away

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Men. 5.3.5 (Lewis & Short); Ter. Hec. 3.4.10

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; in ōrātiōne Cicerōnis rāra)

    To run off, take to one’s heels; mostly in comedy (Lewis & Short).

  • effugium, effugiī n. — an escape; a way of escape

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Liv. 23.1.8: dare effugium (Lewis & Short); Traupman 310

    For “escape” as a noun, Latin more often says fuga, flight, or uses the verb.

  • sē in pedēs conjicere — take to one’s heels

    conjiciō with the reflexive and in pedēs · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 1.4.13 (Lewis & Short), s.v. conjiciō; Traupman 100

    (vōx cōmica: Ter.; Plaut. sē in pedēs cōnferre)

Examples

  • tum vulpēcula ēvāsit puteō nīxa celsīs cornibus hircumque clausō līquit haerentem vadō

    then the little fox got out of the well, climbing on his tall horns, and left the goat stuck in the shut-in waterPhaedr. 4.9.11–12

  • cervus nemorōsīs excitātus latibulīs, ut vēnātōrum effugeret īnstantem necem, caecō timōre proximam vīllam petit

    a stag, roused from his woodland hiding-places, made blindly for the nearest farm to escape the hunters closing inPhaedr. 2.8.1–3

See also escape, away, slip away, capture, avoid.
